fullPassage:
(A) Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. In addition to a variety of other duties, every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. The goal was to raise the reading level of the students with whom she worked to help enable her school to ascend from its "academic emergency" status under the state's education rules. Emma was in one of Sandy's afternoon reading groups, and she was not improving. She lacked patience and often lost focus, at which point she became disruptive, primarily to amuse herself, or so it seemed.

(D) When Emma lost focus, it was difficult for Sandy to teach her or the other six students in the reading group. Sandy spent a lot of time thinking about how she could help Emma keep her focus and be successful. After much reflection, she decided to get her impression of how the reading group was going. When they met later that week, Emma said something that really surprised her. Emma shared that she felt like Sandy needed to be more patient with her when she sounded out words she was reading to the group. Emma knew she was not good at it, and it made her nervous and want to get away from the group.

(B) That evening after school, Sandy reflected on what Emma had said. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to sound out words. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction in addition to the small-group time. In those one-on-one meetings, Sandy let Emma select a book from a handful of books that were at her reading level. Then Sandy would read a paragraph out loud and have Emma read one.

(C) They would continue to swap back and forth. Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability to sound out words improved. Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group with her classmates and started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive or feeling anxious. More than anything, her newfound confidence made her want to try and read other books!

questions.stem: 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) Emma 소개 → (D) Emma의 집중력 문제와 Sandy와의 대화 → (B) Sandy의 해결 방안(일대일 수업) → (C) 결과(향상과 자신감)
det.analysis:

(C): 결과(향상 + 자신감)

questions.passage:
Sandy spent a lot of time thinking about how she could help Emma keep her focus and be successful.

(A) Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to sound out words. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction.

(B) Emma shared that she felt like Sandy needed to be more patient with her when she sounded out words she was reading to the group. Emma knew she was not good at it, and it made her nervous.

(C) After much reflection, she decided to get her impression of how the reading group was going. When they met later that week, Emma said something that really surprised her.
questions.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주어진 문장(해결 방법 고민) → (C) 숙고 후 Emma의 인상을 알아보기로 함 → (B) Emma의 피드백 → (A) 연구 회상 및 일대일 수업 제안
det.analysis:
✅ ④ (C)-(B)-(A)
(C): 숙고 후 Emma와 만남 결정
(B): Emma의 솔직한 피드백
(A): 피드백 후 연구 회상 + 해결책 실행

questions.passage: They would continue to swap back and forth. ① Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. ② Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability to sound out words improved. ③ Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group with her classmates and started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive or feeling anxious. ④ More than anything, her newfound confidence made her want to try and read other books!
questions.stem: 다음 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 곳은? "Emma no longer dreaded reading aloud in front of others."

det.korean: Emma가 더 이상 다른 사람들 앞에서 소리 내어 읽는 것을 두려워하지 않았다는 내용은, 수업에서 방해 행동 없이 끝까지 마쳤다는 ③과 자신감을 얻었다는 ④ 사이에 오는 것이 자연스럽습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③: 수업 완주(③) → 소리 내어 읽기 두려움 극복(삽입문) → 자신감(④)
❌ ①: 아직 향상 시작 단계
❌ ②: 읽기 수준 향상 설명 중
❌ ④: 자신감 이후는 결론이므로 부적절

questions.passage: Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. In addition to a variety of other duties, every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders ①<u>who</u> were reading below grade level. The goal was to raise the reading level of the students with ②<u>who</u> she worked. Emma was in one of Sandy's afternoon reading groups, and she was not ③<u>improving</u>. She ④<u>lacked</u> patience and often lost focus.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② with who → with whom: 전치사(with) 뒤에는 목적격 관계대명사 whom이 와야 합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① who: 주격 관계대명사 (적절)
❌ ② who → whom: 전치사 with + 목적격 관계대명사
✅ ③ improving: was not improving 과거진행형 (적절)
✅ ④ lacked: 과거시제 (적절)
det.tip: 전치사 + 관계대명사: with whom (전치사 뒤에는 목적격 whom 필수)

questions.passage: In those one-on-one meetings, Sandy let Emma ①<u>select</u> a book from a handful of books that ②<u>were</u> at her reading level. Then Sandy would read a paragraph out loud and ③<u>have</u> Emma ④<u>to read</u> one.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ to read → read: 사역동사 have + 목적어 + 동사원형 구조입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① select: let + 목적어 + 동사원형 (적절)
✅ ② were: books(복수) + 과거시제 (적절)
✅ ③ have: 사역동사 (적절)
❌ ④ to read → read: have + 목적어 + 동사원형 (to부정사 불가)
det.tip: 사역동사 have/let/make + 목적어 + 동사원형: to를 쓰지 않는다

questions.passage: Emma shared that she felt like Sandy needed to be more patient with her when she sounded out words she was ________ to the group.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 어법상 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 과거진행형(was reading)의 현재분사 reading이 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② reading: was + reading 과거진행형
❌ ① read: 원형/과거
❌ ③ to read: to부정사
❌ ④ reads: 3인칭 단수 현재
det.tip: was reading: 과거진행형으로 '읽고 있던 중' 표현

questions.passage: The goal was to raise the reading level of the students with whom she worked to help enable her school to __________ from its "academic emergency" status under the state's education rules.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 학교가 '학업 비상' 상태에서 벗어나 올라가는(ascend) 것이 목표였습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ascend: 학업 비상 상태에서 상승/탈출
❌ ② descend: 하강하다 → 반대
❌ ③ withdraw: 철수하다 → 맥락 부적절
❌ ④ benefit: 이익을 얻다 → 어울리지 않음

questions.passage: When they met later that week, Emma said something that really __________ her.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Emma가 한 말이 Sandy를 놀라게 했다(surprised)는 것입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ surprised: Emma의 예상 밖 피드백에 놀람
❌ ① bored: 지루하게 하다 → 맥락 부적절
❌ ② angered: 화나게 하다 → 원문과 다름
❌ ④ disappointed: 실망시키다 → 원문과 다름
det.tip: surprised: Emma의 솔직한 피드백이 예상 밖이었음

questions.passage: That evening after school, Sandy ①<u>reflected</u> on what Emma had said. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to ②<u>decrease</u> the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to sound out words. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some ③<u>one-on-one</u> reading instruction in addition to the small-group time. In those one-on-one meetings, Sandy let Emma ④<u>select</u> a book from a handful of books.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② decrease(줄이다)는 부적절합니다. 원문에서는 읽는 단어 수를 increase(늘리다) 해야 한다고 했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① reflected: 원문 그대로 (적절)
❌ ② decrease → increase: 읽기 향상을 위해 늘려야 함
✅ ③ one-on-one: 원문 그대로 (적절)
✅ ④ select: 원문 그대로 (적절)
det.tip: decrease(줄이다) ↔ increase(늘리다): 읽기 연습량은 늘려야 향상

questions.passage: They would continue to swap back and forth. ①<u>Slowly</u> but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability to sound out words ②<u>declined</u>. Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group with her classmates and started to make it through the ③<u>entire</u> lesson without becoming ④<u>disruptive</u> or feeling anxious.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② declined(감소했다)는 부적절합니다. 원문에서 Emma의 발음 능력은 improved(향상되었다)고 했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① Slowly: 원문 그대로 (적절)
❌ ② declined → improved: 능력이 향상됨
✅ ③ entire: 원문 그대로 (적절)
✅ ④ disruptive: 원문 그대로 (적절)

questions.stem: 다음은 위 글의 요약문이다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? After hearing Emma's honest feedback, Sandy adopted a(n) (A)__________ approach to reading instruction, which led to significant (B)__________ in Emma's reading skills and classroom behavior.

det.korean: (A) individualized(개별화된) - (B) improvement(향상): Sandy는 개별 맞춤 접근법을 채택해 Emma의 읽기와 행동이 향상되었습니다.

❌ ② (A) group-based - (B) improvement
❌ ④ (A) individualized - (B) regression
